title: Morning Edition
dek: Iran has put a seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal on the table while Washington signals rejection; Bangkok is under citywide flood emergency; a New Mexico jury found Meta deceived users; and an old Aristotelian idea asks whether character sometimes improves by overshooting.

lead_story.headline: Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, but the U.S. appears unwilling to take the deal
lead_story.summary: Iran says a proposal sent through Qatari mediators would reopen Hormuz and end hostilities within seven days if Washington lifts its blockade and reduces military pressure. Reuters reported Saturday that Iran was awaiting a U.S. response after the Wall Street Journal said President Donald Trump had rejected the proposal; Tehran says nuclear concessions are not part of the offer.
lead_story.why_it_matters: Hormuz remains one of the world economy’s most consequential chokepoints. A workable agreement could reduce war and energy-market risk quickly; rejection leaves a diplomatic opening but no settlement.

items.headline: Bangkok declared all 50 districts disaster-affected after nearly 300 mm of rain in 48 hours
items.summary: Torrential rain flooded major roads and filled canals. Thai reporting says flooding remains across 21 provinces and more than 84,000 people are affected nationally.
items.why_it_matters: The immediate problem is drainage and emergency access; the larger one is how a low-lying megacity manages disruptive rainfall at metropolitan scale.

items.headline: A New Mexico jury found Meta deceived Facebook users about privacy protections
items.summary: After a two-week Santa Fe trial, jurors found Meta violated New Mexico consumer-protection law through deceptive statements about user data and platform practices. The judge will determine penalties later; Meta disputes the verdict.
items.why_it_matters: New Mexico’s case tests how old platform promises can generate present liability.

items.headline: India ordered states to crack down on nicotine pouches
items.summary: India’s health ministry told states to act against oral nicotine pouches sold outside the drug-approval framework, following earlier state enforcement.
items.why_it_matters: India is treating pouches as unapproved drug products rather than simply another tobacco category.

items.headline: Recent miss: Pakistan and Afghanistan slid into another round of cross-border fighting
items.summary: Pakistan says 13 Afghan Taliban personnel were killed in an overnight border clash; Kabul disputes that account. The exchange followed Pakistani air and drone strikes inside Afghanistan earlier in the week.
items.why_it_matters: Repeated strikes, drones and retaliation are making direct state-on-state escalation easier even as the TTP sanctuary dispute remains unresolved.

items.headline: Older catch-up: the children exposed to 9/11 dust are finally getting a dedicated long-term health study
items.summary: Roughly 25,000 children lived or attended school near the World Trade Center when the towers fell, yet few entered early government follow-up cohorts. A congressionally funded CDC effort is now being organized.
items.why_it_matters: It shows why disaster surveillance has to begin before latent harms are known.

items.headline: Can becoming better sometimes require deliberately overshooting the virtue you want?
items.summary: Philosopher Sabrina B. Little revisits Aristotle’s image of straightening warped timber: if character bends too far toward one vice, improvement may require temporarily pushing toward the opposite extreme.
items.why_it_matters: Overcorrection can expose where balance lies, but can also replace one failure with another.

items.headline: Calliaqua brought back its Culture Pot for an evening of food, craft and local performance
items.summary: The Calliaqua community in St. Vincent and the Grenadines brought its Culture Pot back Friday evening, filling the town square with local food, art, craft and entertainment under the theme “One Pot, Many Flavours.”
items.why_it_matters: Nothing globally consequential: it is a small glimpse of a town making room for people to cook, sell things, perform and spend an evening together.
items.source: NBC Radio St. Vincent and the Grenadines
items.country: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines — Calliaqua

worth_your_time.headline: Watch scientists decipher burned scrolls without unrolling them
worth_your_time.summary: Researchers carbonized replica papyri to test whether tiny amounts of lead in ancient-style ink can be detected by X-rays, potentially helping virtual-unwrapping teams find writing inside some unopened Herculaneum scrolls.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: The team recreated the damage process before applying the method to irreplaceable artifacts.
